key_insight: Machine learning on longitudinal EHR data can surface prediagnostic signals for several rare genetic diseases years before the first diagnostic code appears.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help clinicians prioritize patients for earlier review and confirmatory genetic testing, potentially shortening the diagnostic odyssey.
method: Trained ML models on billing codes and phenotypes extracted from clinical notes.
Applied the models across eight rare conditions in a longitudinal cohort of about 3 million Mayo Clinic patient records.
Compared early identification performance at 99% specificity and measured lead time before first diagnostic billing code.
evidence_signal: Across eight conditions, early identification ranged from 10% to 89% at 99% specificity, with median lead times often exceeding one year and reaching 2,755 days for hereditary angioedema.
watch_item: Performance varies substantially by condition, so real-world use will need careful validation, workflow integration, and attention to false-positive burden.
paper_title: Early identification of rare disease using deep phenotyping of electronic health records
